title.narrative: Improving Growth Corridors in Mindanao Road Sector Project

description.narrative:
The project will improve an estimated 280 kilometers (km) of national primary, secondary, and tertiary roads in Mindanao. The improvements will include paving earth roads, replacing damaged road sections, widening existing roads, adding surface overlays, and replacing and strengthening bridges. The project roads will be designed with features to strengthen resilience to climate change. Among the structural and non-structural features included are elevated pavement levels, enhanced slope protection, and improved maintenance of drainage structures. Road safety on these roads will be improved through road safety community awareness campaigns. The project will finance detailed engineering for improvement of another 300 km of national highways in Mindanao, to be implemented under future projects. The Government will determine the roads for which the detailed design will be prepared. The design will incorporate features to strengthen resilience to climate change.
The project will improve the institutional capacity of DPWH to make management of the transport sector more efficient and contribute to improved operations of the transport sector in Mindanao and nationwide. Strengthening of DPWH's institutional capacity will take place in regional offices and in headquarters. Training in multi-year planning carried out exclusively in DPWH regional offices, while the new human resource database system integrating all DPWH operations will be made operational in all DPWH offices. Making the new online system for budgeting and fiscal monitoring operational and the provision of support in supervising regional planning will take place in DPWH headquarters.

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1: Civil Works. As of January 2025, the overall project implementation progress has reached 88.25%, with 84.81% of the total project time elapsed. For the core subprojects, three road projects have been completed. For the non-core subprojects, eight road and bridge projects are ongoing, with all contracts already awarded and showing varying levels of physical progress. In addition, a new subproject (SP8A) located in Sulu, spanning 6.4 kilometers, is planned to be added. The subproject is currently undergoing completion of due diligence, with construction targeted to begin in September 2025.Output 2: Feasibility Study (FS) and Detailed Engineering Design (DED) for Future Projects. The feasibility study is nearly complete, while the detailed engineering design (DED) is still ongoing. As of April 2025, the DED has reached 89.92% completion and is on track to be fully completed by June 2025.Output 3: Strengthening DPWH's Capacity in Transport Sector Management at Both Headquarters and Regional Levels. Under Output 3, several institutional capacity development (ICD) activities are being implemented. ICD 1, which focuses on training for multi-year planning, was contracted in November 2024. ICD 2, which supports fiscal monitoring and regional planning, is currently ongoing. ADB has approved the Invitation for Bids (IFB) and the final bidding documents, and the IFB was published on both the ADB and DPWH websites, with a submission deadline of 14 May 2025. Meanwhile, ICD 3, focused on developing a human resource database system for DPWH is experiencing delays. On 14 April 2025, ADB issued a no-objection to the executing agency's list of prospective bidders and allowed the process to proceed using limited competitive bidding, as recommended by the Procurement Planning and Facilitation Division (PPFD).
Issue 1: Coordination Gaps Between DPWH Headquarters and Regional Offices. Some roads and bridges originally included in the project were later cancelled because they were already being implemented by DPWH regional offices. This reflects a lack of coordination between the central and regional levels. The Institutional Capacity Development (ICD) activities under the project aim to address this issue. As part of these efforts, it is recommended to upgrade DPWH's existing multi-year planning system and institutionalize its use across all offices nationwide to ensure better alignment. Improving planning tools and strengthening data management systems will also help prevent future overlaps and duplications in project implementation.
Issue 2: Delays in RIPP (Resettlement and Indigenous Peoples Plan) Implementation. For non-core subprojects, the implementation of social safeguards, particularly the RIPP, is falling behind the progress of civil works. This misalignment can lead to risks and complications during construction. To address this, it is important to streamline internal processes and strengthen coordination between DPWH offices and other relevant agencies. Improving the management of the Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) and ensuring better legal support will also help. In addition, ADB provides technical assistance to accelerate the timely and effective implementation of the RIPP.
